gap: No result ChatGPT got states, in a form we could open and check, which kind of wall switch each Lumary gimbal can be wired behind. The one maker exclusion we could read, that the RGBAI Gimbal Pro 'isn't compatible with touch dimmer switches' and joins only 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, sits on a lumaryusa.com page that ChatGPT got at rank 12 but did not cite. It probably also appears on the cited lumarysmart.com page for the same product, but we could not open that page to check.
standout_why: I could not open the cited rival pages. lumarysmart.com (RGBAI Pro, 9W gimbal, eyeball gimbal), bestbuy.com, wayfair.com and cloudybaylighting.com all returned HTTP 429 or timed out on repeated tries, and walmart.com showed a bot wall. ChatGPT's own answers already say most of these use 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and that Wi-Fi models 'generally aren't designed for traditional dimmer switches'. So the 2.4 GHz limit and the general dimmer warning are already partly covered. What the rivals lack, as far as we can see, is the maker's exact exclusion (touch dimmers) for a named model, plus a per-model table of switch, housing and ecosystem compatibility. I could not build that table, so this finding adds little over what the rivals say.
decides: It does not change the pick. It confirms one install condition for the RGBAI Pro: it needs a 2.4 GHz network, Lumary names touch dimmer switches as not compatible, and it ships with its own junction box, which makes it a canless install. For the other models (9W 40° tilt, 7W 90° tilt, Ultra, 6-inch, CloudyBay 6-inch) we have no sourced switch or housing exclusions yet, so the page cannot yet say which one suits a home with existing dimmers or cans.
